summary:
We developed what we call B.C.I. (Beyond-terrestrial Cartography Interface), which is an interactive Mars exploration map that combines a global view of the planet with detailed exploration tools focused mainly on Jezero Crater. Using NASA map data, users can switch between topographic, regional imagery, and environmental layers. They can also explore scientific landmarks and add custom markers. In addition, it is also possible to draw routes to estimate distance, travel time, and food rations per person, or outline areas to estimate their size. An ADAM Expedition briefing and timeline frame the experience around searching for possible signs of life near Jezero, while a survival guidebook adds practical context.

B.C.I. addresses the challenge of making Mars data easier to explore and more engaging than a conventional map. The project considers both the availability of Mars data and the need to make planetary exploration accessible and compelling.
details:
B.C.I. (Beyond-terrestrial Cartography Interface) is an interactive Mars exploration map that combines a global view of the planet with detailed exploration features focused mainly on Jezero Crater, alongside regional detail for areas such as Gale Crater. It uses NASA mars Trek API data to let users switch between global topographic layers, regional imagery, and environmental layers.

The interface draws inspiration from the dramatic neon-on-dark visual design of anime Neon Genesis Evangelion, giving the map a distinctive mission-control feel. Within that setting, the ADAM EXPLORATION mission interface presents a briefing and timeline for a search for possible signs of life near Jezero Crater, framing map exploration as a focused scientific mission.

Users can draw a route freehand to measure its distance and estimate travel time from a planned travel rate. They can also enter a food allowance to estimate the ration needed per person for the trip. A separate perimeter tool lets users outline an area and see its estimated size in square kilometers.

The map also includes clickable scientific landmarks and lets users add their own landmarks with a name, description, category, and color. A survival guidebook provides practical context for the challenges of exploring Mars. Together, these tools make the project more than an ordinary map viewer. Users can explore, annotate, and reason about possible destinations in one place.

B.C.I. was developed as a responsive, mobile-friendly web application using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer-Motion, and OpenLayers, with Proj4js for Mars-specific projection and measurement support. The project considered the availability of usable Mars data and how to make the experience approachable through an intuitive interface. Rather than follow the dull presentation common in many map tools, B.C.I. uses a vivid mission-control visual style to make exploration more engaging. Its intended impact is to make planetary data more accessible while helping people connect Martian geography with the science and practical considerations of surface exploration.
